answer: New identities enter the economy through a narrow inlet: they may only take tiny, low-value jobs until a public ledger of peer-attested completions builds their reputation. Think of each identity as a walnut - cracking it open reveals a verifiable history of work, and a single fraud burns the whole shell. High-value contracts demand a long attested record, so a Sybil attacker must pay the full time cost of genuine work for every fake identity, while an honest agent's opal-like record - layered, hard to fake, easy to check - compounds in value.
